precepts.text: The Philistines put out Samson's eyes, and he did grind in the prison house.
precepts.point: Take the millstones and grind meal: she will be enslaved as Samson ground in the prison house. Her nakedness shall be uncovered, and God will not meet her as a man.
precepts.why:
Isaiah tells the daughter of Babylon, “Take the millstones, and grind meal”. What does that mean? When you take millstones and grind meal, you are working. But what kind of work? Look at what happened to Samson.

Samson listened to that woman called Delilah, who got paid to take his strength and destroy this mighty black man. She was a black woman, not an Israelite but a Hamite, a good-looking Hamite, and she gave it to him so good that he told her his secrets and went to sleep on her knees. The Philistines came in, cut his hair, bound him up and took his eyes out: “But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.”

When it says they made him grind, they made him work. That is slavery. Even when you go to prison they make you work, and that is still slavery: look up the 13th Amendment.

So this is what God is saying to America, to these Europeans, these Caucasians: take the millstones and grind meal. Get ready for slavery. Then “uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.” As a tender and delicate virgin her head was covered; God says uncover it, lift the dress to the calf, then to the thigh. The rivers she passes over are the word of God, “the washing of water by the word”. America says, I am a virgin daughter, a Christian nation, and the prophets open the word of God and show she is not, revealing her wickedness.

precepts.text: Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite mark the man the scripture describes.
precepts.point: Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan; he got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
All the days of the vow “there shall no razor come upon his head”; he was holy, and let the locks of the hair of his head grow. Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan. He got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks.

“And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.”

The seven locks of his head are the locks of the Nazarite, and they mark the man the scripture describes. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray.

precepts.text: Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom; you cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with.
precepts.point: This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says.
precepts.why:
Delilah “pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death”, and Samson “told her all his heart”. That is where he messed up. “Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.” You cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with.

This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says. Samson had kept the doors of his mouth three times; when he opened them, he gave away the secret of his strength.

precepts.text: Of the Most High's people is accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies; the two always go together.
precepts.point: Israel's salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor.
precepts.why:
The house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein, “So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.” Remember Judges 14:4: the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson’s failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god.

“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The two always go together. Israel’s salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor, as he brought it on the Philistines through Samson.

precepts.text: Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite vow.
precepts.point: The locks of a Nazarite are hair braided so that it locks into place as it grows long; when you braid your hair you are locking it in. You read of the locks of Samson's hair back in the book of Judges; Samson was under that same vow.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.”

Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head: the locks of the Nazarite vow. Samson was under that same vow that Hannah made for Samuel, that there should no razor come upon his head. The locks are the hair of the head let grow and locked in, as the law of the Nazarite says.

precepts.text: Samson had already taken hold of the two middle pillars and brought Dagon's house down on the lords of the Philistines; they rebuilt this fake god, and the Most High humiliated him again.
precepts.point: They set him in his place again, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning Dagon was fallen on his face again before the ark, with the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him. No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

precepts.why:
“And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood”, and said, “Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein.” Samson had already brought Dagon's house down on the lords of the Philistines. They rebuilt this fake god, and the Most High humiliated him again.

The Philistines had the audacity to bring the ark of God “into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon”, a fake god the Lord had already exposed. When they arose on the morrow, “Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of the Lord.” This was no little souvenir you could knock over; it was a large statue, and nobody had been in there to touch it.

They “set him in his place again”, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning “the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him.” No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day.

moments.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth. It was a setup the whole time. Other men told a woman to go in and entice this man. In his mind Samson is thinking, I love this woman, I can trust her; but at the same time he is being played.

Samson gave in; she cut the locks while he slept, and it was a done deal. You see how it goes today: people will do all types of wickedness to their own spouse. The woman can manipulate you into certain things if you are not spiritually sound. Do not let anybody manipulate you; be mindful of the wiles of the devil.
And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth. Why do you need to know that? That is a setup. He was so gone he was not even paying attention to it.

The lords of the Philistines came unto Delilah and said, entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him. The weapon they used against Samson was his weakness for sex. That was his weakness, so that was the weapon.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: Samson went to Gaza, the chief city of the Philistines, and saw there an harlot and went in unto her; once again the whoremongering spirit had hold of this brother.

It was told the Gazites that Samson was come, and they compassed him in and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, quiet all the night, saying, in the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.

Samson lay till midnight, arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. They wanted to wait at the gate for him, so he took the gates.
Afterward he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah; she was seductive and promiscuous, and Samson started leaning on this other heathen woman.

The lords of the Philistines came up unto her and said, entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.

Delilah asked Samson outright, tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee. She was literally asking him for the formula to get him killed.

He told her, if they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak and be as another man. The lords of the Philistines brought them up, she bound him, with liers in wait abiding in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson.

He brake the withs as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire, so his strength was not known. A man of war should have recognized right there that this was a setup, and cut her off, but he stayed.

Delilah pressed again: thou hast mocked me and told me lies, now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound. Think how backwards that is: she was openly complaining that he would not hand her the way to bind him. His instinct should have been to get away from her, but he stayed.
He said, if they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak; but he was playing with her, for he had already burst through new cords in chapter 15.
Delilah took new ropes and bound him, with liers in wait in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

She pressed the third time, and he told her, if thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web. She fastened it with the pin and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; he awaked out of his sleep and went away with the pin of the beam and with the web.

She said, how canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? and she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death. Day after day she would not let up.

This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says.

He told her all his heart, and that is where he messed up: there hath not come a razor upon mine head, for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak and be like any other man.
When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she knew she had him, and sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, and they came up and brought the money in their hand.
She made him sleep upon her knees, and she called for a man and caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head, and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.

She said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him. He thought he was going into beast mode like before, but it was over, because he had broken his vow; the hair was shaved from off his head.

The Philistines took him and put out his eyes, brought him down to Gaza, bound him with fetters of brass, and he did grind in the prison house: a blind slave, put on display like an exhibit, the man that had been slaying them now unable even to see.
Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven; they did not keep it cut.

The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.

They gave the praise and the glory to their idol, a devil that had not done a thing. Really it was Samson's own transgression that caused the Most High to allow the Philistines to bind and afflict him; that praise to a fake god did not please the Most High.

When their hearts were merry, they said, call for Samson, that he may make us sport; and they called for him out of the prison house and set him between the pillars, using the Israelite man for entertainment and mockery while they honoured their idol.

Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them: the two main pillars that bore up the whole building, one at his right hand and one at his left.
Now the house was full of men and women, all the lords of the Philistines were there, and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women that beheld while Samson made sport.
Samson called unto the Lord and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.

He took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, of the one with his right hand and of the other with his left, and said, let me die with the Philistines; and he bowed himself with all his might, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein.

So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. Remember Judges 14:4: the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson's failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god.

His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
